 Appearance:

Shri Pramod Choubey, learned counsel for the applic
 Shri Surendra Kumar Gupta, learned Public Prosecuto
 respondent/State.
 Ms. Ayushi Thakur, learned counsel for the complain
 Order

This first bail application under Section 482 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (equivalent to Section 438 of Cr.P.C.) has been filed by the applicant-Dheeraj Anjana S/o Shri Ratan Singh for grant of anticipatory bail, who is apprehending his arrest in connection with Crime No.506/2024 registered at Police Station Nanakheda, District Ujjain (M.P.) for commission of offence under Sections 109(1), 296, 351(2), 3(5) of BNS, 2023.
2. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the crime.
Complainant and the applicant are cousins.
Due to some altercation on the dispute of way, the incident had taken place.
The applicant has not fired and none is injured.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:9666 2 MCRC-13324-2025
Sufficient evidence is not available on record to establish the complicity of the accused with the alleged crime.
There is no likelihood of his absconding or tampering with evidence.
He will cooperate with the investigation.
On these contentions, learned counsel prays for allowing the application for grant of anticipatory bail.
3. Learned counsel for the Objector pleads no objection.
4. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent / State has also vehemently opposed the prayer on the ground that applicant has fired from gun and luckily the complainant escaped.
The applicant has been named in the FIR and there are direct allegations against him.
The applicant has one criminal antecedent under Sections 420 and 406 of IPC therefore, prays for dismissal of the application.

sentences.text: 5. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.

6. In the aforesaid factual backdrop, looking to the criminal antecedents, named FIR and role attributed to the applicant, this Court is not inclined to grant benefit of anticipatory bail to the applicant.
Accordingly, the anticipatory bail application filed under Section 482 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 is dismissed.
7 . At this stage, applicant may surrender and may raise all grounds before the trial Court in the regular bail application.
